claims.text: Premelting and melting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are governed by differential atomic diffusion during heating that causes selective surface segregation.
Cu has a relatively low melting point and reduction potential compared with the other alloy constituents.
Elements with lower melting points and lower reduction potentials, particularly Cu, preferentially migrate to the nanoparticle surface during heating.
Cu enrichment at the surface initiates localized premelting.
Co and/or Cr have relatively high surface energies.
High-surface-energy elements such as Co and/or Cr accumulate in a sub-surface layer during heating.
A high-surface-energy-element-enriched sub-surface layer can stabilize surface atoms.
The transient sub-surface layer raises the local melting barrier and retards complete melting.
The initial nanoparticles are homogeneous, disordered solid solutions with a typically FCC structure.
An inert heating environment prevents oxidation and ensures that observed changes arise solely from thermal effects.
Heating produces a transient gradient consisting of a Cu-enriched surface and a Co/Cr-enriched sub-surface.
Relative to a homogeneous baseline, the particles will exhibit earlier localized premelting at Cu-enriched surface regions.
Formation of the stabilizing sub-surface layer will increase the effective melting temperature relative to a homogeneous baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies principally to nanoparticles on the order of tens of nanometers, where surface diffusion and segregation are significant.
The mechanism may not apply to extremely small clusters, bulk materials, or systems dominated by external fields or substrate interactions.
Failure to observe significant segregation during premelting, or failure of the sub-surface layer to correlate with a higher effective melting temperature, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Both the tested particles and the stated baseline are initially homogeneous and lack preexisting segregation, with no distinct baseline treatment specified. Under the proposed heating mechanism, both should develop segregation, so the claimed comparison against a homogeneous baseline is not operationally separated.
